Because the role can perform the RunInstances action in the us- east- 1 region, the user, upon assuming the role, can create a new instance in the us- east- 1 region but cannot perform any other actions. StartInstances starts an existing instance but doesn’t launch a new one.

question: Several objects in a S3 bucket are encrypted using a KMS customer master key. Which of the following will give an IAM user permission to decrypt these objects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the user to the key policy as a key user.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Grant the user access to the key using an IAM policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the user to the key policy as a key administrator.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the user as a principal to the bucket policy.

book_explanation: Granting a user access to use a KMS key to decrypt data requires adding the user to the key policy as a key user. Adding the user as a key administrator is insufficient to grant this access, as is granting the user access to the key using an IAM policy. Adding the user to a bucket policy can grant the user permission to access encrypted objects in the bucket but doesn’t necessarily give the user the ability to decrypt those objects.

question: You run a public- facing application on EC2 instances. The application is backed by a data- base running on RDS. Users access it using multiple domain names that are hosted in Route 53. You want to get an idea of what IP addresses are accessing your application. Which of the following would you stream to CloudWatch Logs to get this information?
book_explanation: VPC flow logs record source IP address information for traffic coming into your VPC. DNS query logs record the IP addresses of DNS queries, but those won’t necessarily be the same IP addresses accessing your application. Because users won’t directly connect to your RDS instance, RDS logs won’t record their IP addresses. CloudTrail logs can record the source IP address of API requests but not connections to an EC2 instance.

question: You’re running a web server that keeps a detailed log of web requests. You want to determine which IP address has made the most requests in the last 24 hours. What should you do to accomplish this? (Choose two.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stream the web server logs to CloudWatch Logs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upload the web server log to S3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Athena to query the data.

book_explanation: Athena lets you perform advanced SQL queries against data stored in S3. A metric filter can increment based on the occurrence of a value in a CloudWatch log group but can’t tell you the most frequently occurring IP address.

question: An application running on an EC2 instance has been updated to send large amounts of data to a server in your datacenter for backup. Previously, the instance generated very little traffic. Which GuardDuty finding type is this likely to trigger?
book_explanation: The Behavior finding type is triggered by an instance sending abnormally large amounts of data or communicating on a protocol and port that it typically doesn’t. The Backdoor finding type indicates that an instance has resolved a DNS name associated with a command- and- control server or is communicating on TCP port 25. The Stealth finding type is triggered by weakening password policies or modifying a CloudTrail configuration. The ResourceCon- sumption finding type is triggered when an IAM user launches an EC2 instance when they’ve never done so.

question: You’ve set up an AWS Config managed rule to check whether a particular security group is attached to every instance in a VPC. You receive an SNS notification that an instance is out of compliance. But when you check the instance a few hours later, the security group is attached. Which of the following may help explain the apparent discrepancy? (Choose two.)
book_explanation: The AWS Config timeline will show every configuration change that occurred on the instance, including the attachment and detachment of security groups. CloudTrail management event logs will also show the actions that detached and attached the secu- rity group. Although AWS Config rules use Lambda functions, the Lambda logs for AWS managed rules are not available to you. VPC flow logs capture traffic ingressing a VPC, but not API events.

question: You want to use Amazon Inspector to analyze the security posture of your EC2 instances running Windows. Which rules package should you not use in your assessment?
book_explanation: The Security Best Practices rules package has rules that apply to only Linux instances. The other rules contain rules for both Windows and Linux instances.

question: You have a distributed application running in datacenters around the world. The applica- tion connects to a public Simple Queue Service (SQS) endpoint to send messages to a queue. How can you prevent an attacker from using this endpoint to gain unauthorized access to the queue? (Choose two.)
book_explanation: You can use an IAM policy or SQS access policy to restrict queue access to certain principals or those coming from a specified IP range. You cannot use network access control lists or security groups to restrict access to a public endpoint.

question: You’re using a public-f acing application load balancer to forward traffic to EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. What can you do to ensure users on the Internet can reach the load balancer over HTTPS without reaching your instances directly? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a security group that allows all inbound traffic to TCP port 443.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach the security group to the instances.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach the security group to the load balancer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the Internet gateway from the VPC.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create a security group that allows all inbound traffic to TCP port 80.

book_explanation: HTTPS traffic traverses TCP port 443, so the security group should allow inbound access to this protocol and port. HTTP traffic uses TCP port 80. Because users need to reach the ALB but not the instances directly, the security group should be attached to the ALB. Removing the Internet gateway would prevent users from reaching the ALB as well as the EC2 instances directly.

question: You’re running a UDP- based application on an EC2 instance. How can you protect it against a DDoS attack?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place the instance behind a network load balancer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implement a security group to restrict inbound access to the instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place the instance behind an application load balancer.

book_explanation: A security group to restrict inbound access to authorized sources is sufficient to guard against a UDP- based DDoS attack. Elastic load balancers do not provide UDP listeners, only TCP. AWS Shield is enabled by default and protects against those UDP- based attacks from sources that are allowed by the security group.

question: You’re running a web application on six EC2 instances behind a network load balancer. The web application uses a MySQL database. How can you protect your application against SQL injection attacks? (Choose two.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign elastic IP addresses to the instances.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place the instances behind an application load balancer.

book_explanation: WAF can block SQL injection attacks against your application, but only if it’s behind an application load balancer. It’s not necessary for the EC2 instances to have an elastic IP address. Blocking access to TCP port 3306, which is the port that MySQL listens on for data- base connections, may prevent direct access to the database server but won’t prevent a SQL injection attack.

question: Which services protect against an HTTP flood attack?
book_explanation: Both WAF and Shield Advanced can protect against HTTP flood attacks, which are marked by excessive or malformed requests. Shield Advanced includes WAF at no charge. Shield Standard does not offer protection against Layer 7 attacks. GuardDuty looks for signs of an attack but does not prevent one.

question: Your security policy requires that you use a KMS key for encrypting S3 objects. It further requires this key be rotated once a year and revoked when misuse is detected. Which key type should you use? (Choose two.)
book_explanation: You can revoke and rotate both a customer- managed CMK and a customer- provided key at will. You can’t revoke or rotate an AWS- managed CMK or an S3-m anaged key.

question: A developer is designing an application to run on AWS and has asked for your input in deciding whether to use a SQL database or DynamoDB for storing highly transactional appli- cation data. Your security policy requires all application data to be encrypted and encryption keys to be rotated every 90 days. Which AWS service should you recommend for storing application data? (Choose two.)
book_explanation: Customer- managed Customer Master Keys (CMKs) can be rotated at will, whereas AWS- managed CMKs are rotated only once a year. RDS and DynamoDB let you use a customer- managed CMK to encrypt data. RedShift is not designed for highly transactional databases and is not appropriate for the application. KMS stores and manages encryption keys but doesn’t store application data.

question: You need to copy the data from an unencrypted EBS volume to another region and encrypt it. How can you accomplish this? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an encrypted snapshot of the unencrypted volume.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simultaneously encrypt and copy the snapshot to the destination region.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Copy the encrypted snapshot to the destination region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an unencrypted snapshot of the unencrypted volume.

book_explanation: To encrypt data on an unencrypted EBS volume, you must first take a snapshot. The snapshot will inherit the encryption characteristics of the source volume, so an unencrypted EBS volume will always yield an unencrypted snapshot. You can then simultaneously encrypt the snapshot as you copy it to another region.

question: An instance with an unencrypted EBS volume has an unencrypted EFS filesystem mounted on it. You need to encrypt the data on an existing EFS filesystem using a KMS key. How can you accomplish this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encrypt the EBS volume of the instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a new encrypted EFS filesystem and copy the data to it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable encryption on the existing EFS filesystem.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a third-p arty encryption program to encrypt the data.

book_explanation: You can enable encryption on an EFS filesystem only when you create it; therefore, the only option to encrypt the data using KMS is to create a new EFS filesystem and copy the data to it. A third- party encryption program can’t use KMS keys to encrypt data. Encrypting the EBS volume will encrypt the data stored on the volume, but not on the EFS filesystem.

question: On which of the following can you not use an ACM-g enerated TLS certificate? (Choose two.)
book_explanation: You can install an ACM- generated certificate on a CloudFront distribution or applica- tion load balancer. You can’t export the private key of an ACM- generated certificate, so you can’t install it on an EC2 instance. AWS manages the TLS certificates used by S3.

question: Which of the following assesses the security posture of your AWS resources against AWS best practices?
book_explanation: Security Hub checks the configuration of your AWS services against AWS best practices.

question: Which of the following best describes the AWS Free Tier?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Free access to AWS services for a new account’s first month

choices.label: B
choices.text: Free access to all instance types of AWS EC2 instances for new accounts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free access to basic levels of AWS services for a new account’s first year

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unlimited and open-e nded access to the “free tier” of most AWS services

book_explanation: The Free Tier provides free access to basic levels of AWS services for a new account’s first year.

question: Which of the following storage classes provides the least expensive storage and transfer rates?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amazon S3 One Zone- Infrequent Access

book_explanation: Standard provides the most replicated and quickest- access service and is, therefore, the most expensive option. Storage rates for Standard- Infrequent and One Zone-I nfrequent are lower than Standard but are still more expensive than Glacier.

question: Which AWS service is best suited to controlling your spending by sending email alerts?
book_explanation: Cost Explorer provides usage and spending data. Organizations lets you combine multiple AWS accounts under a single administration. TCO Calculator would let you compare the costs of running an application on AWS versus locally, but it no longer exists.

question: Your AWS infrastructure is growing and you’re beginning to have trouble keeping track of what you’re spending. Which AWS service is best suited to analyzing account usage data at scale?
book_explanation: Cost Explorer provides usage and spending data, but without the ability to easily incor- porate Redshift and QuickSight that Cost and Usage Reports offers. Trusted Advisor checks your account for best-p ractice compliance. Budgets allows you to set alerts for problem- atic usage.

question: Your company wants to more closely coordinate the administration of its multiple AWS accounts, and AWS Organizations can help it do that. How does that change your security profile? (Choose three.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: An organization- level administration account breach is potentially more damaging.

choices.label: B
choices.text: User permissions can be controlled centrally at the organization level.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You should upgrade to use only specially hardened organization- level VPCs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standard security best practices such as MFA and strong passwords are even more essential.

choices.label: E
choices.text: You should upgrade all of your existing security groups to account for the changes.

book_explanation: As efficient as Organizations can be, so does the threat they represent grow. There is no such thing as a specially hardened organization- level VPC. Security groups don’t require any special configuration.

question: Which of the following resource states are monitored by AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: S3 buckets with public read access permissions

choices.label: D
choices.text: EC2 Linux instances that allow root account SSH access

book_explanation: Trusted Advisor monitors your EC2 instances for lower than 10 percent CPU and network I/O below 5 MB on four or more days. Trusted Advisor doesn’t monitor Route 53 hosted zones or the status of S3 data transfers. Proper OS- level configuration of your EC2 instances is your responsibility.

question: You’re planning a new AWS deployment, and your team is debating whether they’ll be better off using an RDS database or one run on an EC2 instance. Which of the following tools will be most helpful?
book_explanation: The Pricing Calculator is the most direct tool for this kind of calculation. TCO Calculator helps you compare costs of on-p remises to AWS deployments. Trusted Advisor checks your account for best- practice compliance. Cost and Usage Reports help you analyze data from an existing deployment.

question: Which of the following is not a metric you can configure an AWS budget to track?
book_explanation: Monitoring of EBS volumes for capacity is not within the scope of budgets.

question: Which of the following statements are true of cost allocation tags? (Choose two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tags can take up to 24 hours before they appear in the Billing and Cost Management dashboard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tags can’t be applied to resources that were launched before the tags were created.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You’re allowed five free budgets per account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You can activate and manage cost allocation tags from the Tag Editor page.

book_explanation: Tags can take up to 24 hours to appear and they can’t be applied to legacy resources. You’re actually allowed only two free budgets per account. Cost allocation tags are managed from the Cost Allocation Tags page.

question: Your online web store normally requires three EC2 instances to handle traffic but experiences a twofold increase in traffic for the two summer months. Which of the following approaches makes the most sense?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run three on-d emand instances 12 months per year and schedule six reserve instances for the summer months.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run three spot instances for the summer months and three reserve instances 12 months/year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run nine reserve instances for 12 months/year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run three reserve instances 12 months/year and purchase three scheduled reserve instances for the summer months.

book_explanation: The most effective approach would be to run three reserve instances 12 months/year and purchase three scheduled reserve instances for the summer. Spot instances are not appropriate because they shut down automatically. Since it’s possible to schedule an RI to launch within a recurring block of time, provisioning other instance configurations for the summer months will be wasteful.

question: Which of the following settings do you not need to provide when configuring a reserved instance?
book_explanation: Interruption polices are relevant to spot instances, not reserved instances. Payment options (All Upfront, Partial Upfront, or No Upfront), reservation types (Standard or Con- vertible RI), and tenancy (Default or Dedicated) are all necessary settings for RIs.

question: Your new web application requires multiple EC2 instances running 24/7 and you’re going to purchase reserved instances. Which of the following payment options is the most expensive when configuring a reserve instance?
book_explanation: No Upfront is the most expensive option. The more you pay up front, the lower the overall cost. There’s no option called Monthly.

question: Which of the following benefits of containers such as Docker can significantly reduce your AWS compute costs? (Choose two.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Containers can deliver increased server density.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Containers make it easy to reliably replicate server environments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Containers can run using less memory than physical machines.

book_explanation: Containers are more dense and lightweight. Containers do tend to launch more quickly than EC2 instances and do make it easy to replicate server environments, but those are not primarily cost savings.

question: Which of the following is the best use of an EC2 reserved instance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An application that will run continuously for six months straight

choices.label: B
choices.text: An application that will run continuously for 36 months straight

choices.label: C
choices.text: An application that runs only during local business hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: An application that runs at unpredictable times and can survive unexpected shutdowns

book_explanation: Standard reserve instances make the most sense when they need to be available 24/7 for at least a full year, with even greater savings over three years. Irregular or partial workdays are not good candidates for this pricing model.

question: Which of the following describes “unused EC2 instances matching a particular set of launch specifications”?
book_explanation: A spot instance pool is made up of unused EC2 instances. There are three request types: Request, Request And Maintain, and Reserve For Duration. A spot instance interrup- tion occurs when the spot price rises above your maximum. A spot fleet is a group of spot instances launched together.

question: Which of the following best describes a spot instance interruption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A spot instance interruption occurs when the spot price rises above your maximum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A spot instance interruption is the termination of a spot instance when its workload completes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A spot instance interruption occurs when a spot request is manually restarted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A spot instance interruption is the result of a temporary outage in an AWS datacenter.

book_explanation: A spot instance interruption occurs when the spot price rises above your maximum. Workload completions and datacenter outages are never referred to as interruptions. Spot requests can’t be manually restarted.

question: Which of the following describes the maximum instances or vCPUs you want running?
book_explanation: Target capacity represents the maximum instances you want running. A spot instance pool contains unused EC2 instances matching a particular set of launch specifications. Spot maximum and spot cap sound good but aren’t terms normally used in this context.

question: You need to make sure your EBS volumes are regularly backed up, but you’re afraid you’ll forget to remove older snapshot versions, leading to expensive data bloat. What’s the best solution to this problem?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a script that will regularly invoke the AWS CLI to prune older snapshots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an EBS Scheduled Reserved Instance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tie a string to your finger.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle configuration policy to remove old snapshots.

book_explanation: The EBS Lifecycle Manager can be configured to remove older EBS snapshots according to your needs. Creating a script is possible, but it’s nowhere near as simple, and it’s not tightly integrated with your AWS infrastructure. There is no “EBS Scheduled Reserve In- stance” but there is an “EC2 Scheduled Reserve Instance.” Tying a string? Really? EBS snap- shots are stored in S3, but you can’t access the buckets that they’re kept in.

question: Which of these AWS CLI commands will launch a spot fleet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: aws ec2 request- fleet - - spot- fleet- request- config file:// Config.json

choices.label: B
choices.text: aws ec2 spot- fleet - - spot- fleet- request- config file:// Config.json

choices.label: C
choices.text: aws ec2 launch- spot- fleet - - spot- fleet- request- config/ file:// Config.json

choices.label: D
choices.text: aws ec2 request- spot- fleet - - spot- fleet- request- config/ file:// Config.json

book_explanation: The command is request- spot- fleet. The - - spot- fleet- request- config argument points to a JSON configuration file.

question: Which of the following elements is not something you’d include in your spot fleet request?
book_explanation: The availability zone, target capacity, and AMI are all elements of a complete spot fleet request.
